topic: Introduction to speed and velocity, vectors, wind velocity, vector addition and triangle of velocity.
syllabus_extract: Introduction to speed and velocity, vectors, wind velocity, vector addition and triangle of velocity.
specific_objectives: 14.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain and define a position on the earth.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Vector addition diagram drawing; Safety: Ensure sharp pencils are capped; Supervision: Instructor verifies scale accuracy.
intro_questions: What is the difference between speed and velocity?

development.content:
Definition of position on earth
Scalar vs Vector quantities
Speed and velocity definitions
Wind velocity components
Vector addition principles

Triangle of velocity construction
Head-to-tail vector method
Resultant vector calculation
Wind correction angle determination
Ground speed derivation

Interpretation of velocity triangles
Effect of wind direction changes
Magnitude and direction analysis
Real-world flight scenario application
Error sources in vector addition

summary_questions: Explain how wind velocity affects ground speed.
Describe the steps to construct a triangle of velocity.
Differentiate between true airspeed and ground speed.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the navigation components required for the next lesson (LP 05) regarding the triangle of velocities.

pft_rows.syllabus: Introduction to the navigation components of the triangle of velocities i.e. airspeed, Mach nos., ground speed, track and drift. Introduction to the application of the triangle of velocities in navigation.
